chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who lends another man the debased dirhams, and takes back from him the fresh (new) dirhams, which please him. He said, 'There is no harm.' And he mentioned that from Ali (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمَ الطَّازَجِيَّةَ: Fresh or new dirhams (coins with full intrinsic value)
key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمَ الْغِلَّةَ: Debased or worn dirhams (coins with lower intrinsic value)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to repay a loan of debased coins with fresh, high-quality coins in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of repaying a loan of debased currency (ghillah) with fresh, high-quality coins (tazajiyyah), affirming that the creditor cannot demand equal weight or count if the quality differs, provided the debtor acts in good faith. Attributed to Imam Ali (AS), this ruling underscores the flexibility in qard contracts to accommodate economic realities, distinguishing it from strict riba prohibitions by focusing on the absence of exploitation. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on fairness and the practical adaptability of financial transactions within the framework of divine law.
